children.topic: 1. Severe epigastric pain radiating to back (relieved by leaning forward)
2. Serum Lipase or Amylase >3x upper limit of normal (Lipase more specific & remains elevated longer)
3. Characteristic imaging findings on Contrast CT / MRI / US
Physical Signs: Cullen sign (periumbilical ecchymosis), Grey Turner sign (flank ecchymosis), Fox sign (inguinal ligament ecchymosis)
Atlanta Classification: Mild (no organ failure), Moderate (transient organ failure <48h), Severe (persistent organ failure >48h)
Ranson Criteria (at admission & 48h): GALAW & C-HOBIC (Age >55, WBC >16k, Glucose >200, LDH >350, AST >250; Hct drop >10%, BUN rise >5, Ca <8, PaO2 <60, Base deficit >4, Fluid sequestration >6L)
BISAP Score (BEDS): BUN >25, Impaired mental status, SIRS, Age >60, Pleural effusion
CT Severity Index (CTSI / Balthazar): Combines inflammation grade (A-E) + % necrosis (0-50%+)
Initial Therapy: Aggressive IV fluid resuscitation (Ringer's Lactate 200-500 mL/h), early oral feeding as tolerated (low fat), analgesia (Multimodal, NSAIDs/Opioids)
Role of Antibiotics: NO routine prophylactic antibiotics! Only for documented infected necrosis
<4 weeks: Acute Peripancreatic Fluid Collection (APFC) vs Acute Necrotic Collection (ANC)
>4 weeks: Pancreatic Pseudocyst (encapsulated fluid, no necrosis) vs Walled-Off Necrosis (WON)
Infected Necrosis: Step-up approach (Percutaneous/EUS drain → Video-assisted retroperitoneal debridement VARD / Endoscopic necrosectomy → Open necrosectomy)
